title: Unit 3 : Session 12 : SLO 1 — Tutorial: IEEE 754 Single Precision Encoding
sections: Section B: Fill in the Blanks (Understand)
The IEEE 754 single precision format uses 32 bits in total.
The exponent is stored with a bias of 127 in single precision.
The sign bit is 0 for positive numbers and 1 for negative numbers.
The actual exponent is calculated by subtracting the BIAS (127) from the stored exponent.
The mantissa represents the FRACTIONAL part of the normalized binary number.
Section C: Activity — Encode -12.375 in IEEE 754 Single Precision

Roles: Decimal Converter (decimal → binary), Normalizer (1.x × 2^E form), Exponent Encoder (adds bias 127, converts to 8-bit), Sign Bit Decider (0 for +, 1 for -), Mantissa Filler (fraction bits into 23-bit field), Encoder Assembler (combines into the 32-bit word).
Each role passes its result to the next stage, demonstrating how an FPU encodes a decimal value into IEEE 754 format step by step.
